title: Bounded-size modules are cardinal-presentable
statement:
Fix a universe $U$ as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $R$ be a unital ring in $U$, let $\rho\in U$ be an uncountable regular cardinal with $|R|<\rho$, and let $M$ be a left $R$-module in $U$ with $|M|<\rho$. Regular means that unions of fewer than $\rho$ sets each of size less than $\rho$ have size less than $\rho$. A small category is $\rho$-filtered when every diagram with fewer than $\rho$ morphisms admits a cocone. The module $M$ is $\rho$-presentable in $\operatorname{Mod}_R$: for every $U$-small $\rho$-filtered diagram $D$ of left $R$-modules, the canonical map
$$\varinjlim_i\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,D_i)\ \longrightarrow\ \operatorname{Hom}_R(M,\varinjlim_iD_i)$$
is bijective, with colimits as in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. In particular every map to the colimit factors through some stage, and two maps $M\to D_i$ equal in the colimit become equal after one morphism $i\to j$ of the index category.
